info.name: nseutask - Task Manager
info.description:
Task Manager REST API.

**How to use**
1. Import this collection and the `nseutask local` environment, select the environment.
2. Run the collection with the Runner (top to bottom) or send requests one by one.

Tokens are saved into the environment by the login requests and attached automatically: the collection uses Bearer `{{token}}`. Requests of the folder *Access control* switch to `{{otherToken}}` and `{{adminToken}}`.

Every request has tests; error requests check the application error code.

request.description: Application and database liveness.

item.name: 2. Tasks
item.description: CRUD, filters and pagination. Run top to bottom: the requests share {{taskId}} and {{version}}.

request.description: The author is the current user, the status starts as TODO. Saves {{taskId}}, {{version}} and {{userId}}.

exec: pm.test("Location header points to the task", () => pm.expect(pm.response.headers.get("Location")).to.include("/api/tasks/" + json.id));

request.description: Assigns the task to the current user.
Task by id.
All tasks, newest first. Page size is 10 by default, 100 at most.
Only tasks in TODO.

exec: pm.test("All tasks are TODO", () => pm.response.json().content.forEach(t => pm.expect(t.status).to.eql("TODO")));

request.description: Tasks created by the current user.

exec: pm.test("All tasks have this author", () => pm.response.json().content.forEach(t => pm.expect(t.author.id).to.eql(Number(pm.environment.get("userId")))));

request.description: Tasks assigned to the current user.

exec: pm.test("All tasks have this assignee", () => pm.response.json().content.forEach(t => pm.expect(t.assignee.id).to.eql(Number(pm.environment.get("userId")))));
